docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: A national department store seeking relevance with a moderate-income customer
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1166126/000119312510071527/d10k.htm; https://wwd.com/business-news/retail/penneys-dillards-swing-back-to-black-both-see-sales-declines-3216853/
Date: 2010-08-13

J.C. Penney is a US department-store retailer selling apparel, accessories, footwear, home merchandise and related services through mall/off-mall locations and online. The customer proposition combines value, promotions, private brands and national/exclusive labels. This is a merchandising business, not a contracted stream of fixed rent.

The fiscal2009 annual report, filed March30, reports 1,108 department stores. Of these, 416 are owned, including 119 on ground leases. Owning a building on leased land does not give the company an unrestricted freehold land asset. Net property/equipment was US$5.357 billion; no independent current market appraisal is available.

By the Q2 2010 report, the chain has approximately 1,107 locations. Chairman/CEO Myron “Mike” Ullman emphasizes exclusive brands, customer experience and faster merchandise cycles. WWD describes his view that fast-fashion competitors have diverted substantial business from traditional department stores.

The company is adding MNG by Mango shops, with 77 opening initially and an ambition to reach 600 by the end of fall2011. It is also introducing an expanded Liz Claiborne assortment and Call It Spring footwear shops. These are announced contemporary programs with execution risk, not evidence of a future management change.

Apparel and home categories face substitution from discount stores, specialist chains, fast fashion and online retail. Demand depends on product appeal and shopping habits; a cheaper asset valuation alone does not force customers to buy. Promotions can drive traffic while compressing margins, and changing them can alter behavior in uncertain ways.

An investment case could rest on recovery in sales productivity, better assortment, improved inventory turns and expense discipline across an existing store network. The counterargument is that customer relevance and department-store traffic are structurally weakening. Property ownership may provide flexibility, but stores' value often depends on the same retail ecosystem facing pressure.

No completed leadership replacement or outside shareholder operating plan is publicly established at this cutoff. An activist would need to identify specific fixable causes and protect cash during any transition. Recruiting a talented operator is a possible tool, not an operating result that can be presumed in a base case.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Recession damage, pension effects and the reinvestment cycle
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1166126/000119312510071527/d10k.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1166126/000116612610000040/jcpenney10q2nd2010.htm
Date: 2010-09-10

US$ millions except EPS. Fiscal2009 ended January30, 2010. The EPS series is continuing operations; small discontinued-operation differences explain divergence from total net income.

| Metric | FY2007 | FY2008 | FY2009 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net sales | 19,860 | 18,486 | 17,556 |
| Operating income | 1,888 | 1,135 | 663 |
| Reported operating margin | 9.5% | 6.1% | 3.8% |
| Net income | 1,111 | 572 | 251 |
| Diluted continuing EPS | 4.90 | 2.54 | 1.07 |
| Operating cash flow | 1,249 | 1,155 | 1,576 |
| Capital expenditures | 1,243 | 969 | 600 |
| Calculated CFO less capex | 6 | 186 | 976 |
| Common dividends paid | 174 | 178 | 183 |
| Share repurchases | 400 | 0 | 0 |

Sales declined approximately 6.9% in 2008 and 5.0% in 2009. Comparable sales fell 8.5% and 6.3%. The apparent 570-basis-point reported operating-margin decline from 2007 includes a swing from pension income of US$45 million to pension expense US$337 million.

Issuer adjusted operating income was US$1,791 million, US$1,002 million and US$961 million, with adjusted margins 9.0%, 5.4% and 5.5%. The business still has a large performance gap from its own pre-recession level, but not all reported deterioration is a merchandising problem. Issuer adjusted return on beginning invested capital fell from 15.7% to 7.8% across those years; this is the company's non-GAAP definition.

At July31, cash was US$2.003 billion, debt US$3.099 billion and inventory US$3.490 billion. Net debt is US$1.096 billion, calculated. Equity was US$4.886 billion. The cover identifies 236,443,580 shares as of September3.

First-half CFO was negative US$379 million and capex US$229 million, illustrating seasonal inventory and other funding needs. The strong full-year2009 simple FCF should not be annualized from a shrinking-capex/inventory period without normalization.

Q2 operating income was US$95 million on US$3.938 billion sales, approximately 2.4% margin. Cash and property provide runway, not a guarantee that deteriorating sales can be tolerated indefinitely. A clean maintenance-capex split and fully normalized pension cash burden remain diligence items.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: A modest profit recovery accompanied by disappointing guidance
Source: compiled from: https://sgbonline.com/jc-penney-posts-2q-profit-but-outlook-disappoints/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1166126/000116612610000040/jcpenney10q2nd2010.htm; https://www.cnbc.com/2010/09/02/retailers-post-surprisingly-strong-august-sales.html
Date: 2010-09-10

Q2 2010 sales were US$3.938 billion versus US$3.943 billion a year earlier. Comparable sales increased 0.9%, while internet sales increased approximately 4% according to the August earnings coverage. Discontinuing the Big Book catalog contributed to the total-sales comparison.

Net income of US$14 million, US$0.06 diluted EPS, improved from a US$1 million loss. Gross margin rose to 39.4% from 38.5%, but SG&A increased and pension expense remained substantial. The quarter included approximately US$0.05 per share of bond-premium expense related to a debt tender.

The company had already indicated earnings near the low end of the US$0.05–US$0.08 range. The more important disappointment was forward guidance: full-year EPS US$1.40–US$1.50 versus the prior US$1.64 target and approximately US$1.54 analyst expectations in the contemporary Reuters report. Q3 EPS guidance is US$0.16–US$0.20 versus US$0.24 consensus.

Management forecasts Q3 comparable sales up 2–3% and total sales up 1–2%. New exclusive offerings are expected to drive much of the growth. These targets require better customer response, not just cost reduction.

Inventory at July31 rose approximately 7.1% year over year, ahead of sales growth. Management partly attributes this to protecting supply against container shortages from Asia. The alternative interpretation is increased markdown risk if consumer demand disappoints. Either interpretation has consequences for holiday gross margin and working capital.

The latest September2 monthly report provides a positive but incomplete update: August comparable sales rose 2.3%, exceeding the 1.6% analyst estimate reported by CNBC. The company says sales strengthened as school openings approached. Tax-free holidays and promotions helped the broader industry.

The quarterly filing anticipates approximately US$500 million full-year capex, down from US$600 million the prior year. That conserves cash but must be assessed against required systems, store maintenance and growth projects. A turnaround cannot assume permanently minimal investment.

The September improvement does not erase weak second-quarter relative performance. It does show that customers still respond to merchandise and promotions. The central uncertainty is whether new offerings can restore sustainable sales and returns without an expensive, untested reset of the customer proposition.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: Depressed earnings make normalization more important than headline P/E
Source: compiled from: https://exa.ai/library/markets/stock/JCP?date=2010-09-24&view=daily; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1166126/000116612610000040/jcpenney10q2nd2010.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1166126/000119312510071527/d10k.htm; https://wwd.com/business-news/retail/penneys-dillards-swing-back-to-black-both-see-sales-declines-3216853/
Date: 2010-09-24

The historical September24 close is US$25.55, up US$0.95 on the day. The archive gives US$25.66/US$24.87 session high/low and approximately 4.88 million volume. The archive uses a successor issuer name for this old security; no current company valuation is inferred from that label.

The original Yahoo series is unavailable for the delisted symbol. Exact rolling 52-week high/low and average daily volume are not independently reconstructed. WWD reports an August13 US$19.82 close after disappointing guidance; September24 is approximately 28.9% above that observed price, calculated. This is not a claimed 52-week-low comparison.

Using 236.444 million September3 shares, common capitalization is approximately US$6.041 billion. Adding July31 debt of US$3.099 billion and subtracting US$2.003 billion cash gives an indicative US$7.137 billion enterprise value, calculated before pension and other adjustments.

| Basis | Calculated result |
|---|---:|
| FY2009 continuing EPS US$1.07 | 23.9x |
| August2010 EPS guidance US$1.40–US$1.50 | 17.0–18.3x |
| FY2009 issuer adjusted EPS US$1.86 | 13.7x |
| Enterprise value / FY2009 reported operating income US$663m | 10.8x |
| FY2009 CFO less capex US$976m / common value | 16.2% |

The cash-flow yield is unusually high partly because investment spending fell and inventory was reduced. It is not a guaranteed continuing distribution yield. The annual US$0.80 dividend is approximately 3.1% of the price if maintained.

An operational sensitivity illustrates the attraction and risk. Each one-percentage-point operating-margin change on US$17.556 billion sales is approximately US$176 million EBIT before taxes, calculated with sales held constant. Restoring margins therefore matters materially, but fixed sales, no transition cost and unchanged capital are simplifying assumptions, not a forecast.

Owned buildings and some land may offer recovery value, but net property/equipment of US$5.357 billion is neither an appraisal nor incremental value to add to cash-generating store earnings. Ground leases, leased locations, pension obligations and store-level economics complicate a breakup model. Current consensus forward EPS, a historical P/E distribution and matched S&P valuation remain explicit gaps.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Inventory overhang, share loss and the moderate-income consumer
Source: compiled from: http://archive.chicagobreakingbusiness.com/2010/08/slowdown-hits-penney-harder-than-most-retailers-in-2q.html; https://wwd.com/business-news/retail/penneys-dillards-swing-back-to-black-both-see-sales-declines-3216853/; https://www.cnbc.com/2010/09/02/retailers-post-surprisingly-strong-august-sales.html
Date: 2010-09-02

Reuters's August13 account says J.C. Penney has been among the weaker department-store performers, with sales growth lagging Kohl's and Macy's. Its customer tends to have a lower household income and may shift purchases to discount chains and dollar stores when budgets tighten.

CEO Mike Ullman says: “We are taking a relatively conservative approach to the economic climate and especially the moderate consumer.” That explains the outlook but does not distinguish macroeconomic pressure from company-specific loss of relevance.

The report quotes J.P. Morgan analyst Charles Grom: “J.C. Penney’s inventory position looks the least favorable amongst all the department stores we cover, particularly Macy’s.” Inventory grew approximately 7.1% despite nearly flat quarterly sales, raising concern about markdowns and working-capital consumption. Management says part of the build protected against Asian shipping/container shortages.

WWD's August13 report adds a structural challenge: department stores compete with fast-fashion chains such as Zara, Uniqlo, Forever21, H&M and Mango. Faster product cycles and exclusive fashion can divert shoppers even during a general recovery. Ullman responds through shop-in-shops and new brands, but these require investment and customer acceptance.

The distinction matters for a potential management-change thesis. Poor purchasing, marketing or store execution might be repairable. A fundamentally less relevant format or value proposition cannot necessarily be repaired by recruiting a celebrated executive. A new plan must be tested against actual customers rather than inferred from another retailer's success.

The latest counterevidence is August's 2.3% comparable-sales increase, above estimates. CNBC attributes strong industry results partly to promotions, back-to-school demand and tax-free holidays. Customers still shop on major occasions, but they remain value-conscious. A promotion-driven improvement is not proof that promotions can later be removed without losing traffic.

There is no authenticated pre-cutoff activist plan promising a particular CEO, everyday-low-price conversion or new store format. Those are not assumed inevitable catalysts. The bearish case is continued sales underperformance, markdowns and declining capital returns; the opposing case is an established network with recognizable brands, cash and specific merchandising initiatives. Both should be weighed before extrapolating historical peak margins.
docs.D06_peer_and_industry_benchmarks.md:
Title: Direct rivals are capturing a stronger post-recession recovery
Source: compiled from: https://www.macysinc.com/newsroom/news/news-details/2010/Macys-Inc.-Reports-Second-Quarter-Earnings-of-35-Cents-Per-Diluted-Share-Raises-Full-Year-Profit-Guidance-08-11-2010/default.aspx; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/885639/000089271210000604/exh991.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/72333/000119312510187289/dex991.htm; https://wwd.com/business-news/business-features/august-promotions-delivered-sales-3233961/
Date: 2010-09-02

| Chain | Q2 2010 operating evidence | August comparable sales |
|---|---|---:|
| J.C. Penney | Sales US$3.938bn, −0.1%; comps +0.9%; EPS US$0.06 | +2.3% |
| Macy's | EPS US$0.35; reported improved sales, margins and expense rate | +4.3% |
| Kohl's | Sales US$4.1bn, +7.7%; comps +4.6%; EPS US$0.84 | +4.5% |
| Nordstrom | Sales US$2.42bn, +12.7%; comps +8.4%; EPS US$0.66 | +6.3% |

August figures come from WWD's September2 industry report. Same-store definitions and customer mix differ, but the direction is clear: Penney's recovery is materially weaker than these peers'. This supports investigating execution and assortment rather than treating every problem as macroeconomic.

Macy's attributes improvement to My Macy's local assortment, centralized functions, customer focus, exclusive brands, selling skills and store/online integration. These are concrete operational levers rather than a generic claim that a new CEO creates value. Its prior-year reported EPS included restructuring; the cleaner adjusted comparison was US$0.20.

Kohl's management emphasizes market-share gains, inventory discipline and store payroll/marketing leverage. Its updated annual EPS guidance is US$3.57–US$3.70. J.C. Penney's US$1.40–US$1.50 outlook should not be compared dollar-for-dollar as a margin measure, but the stronger same-store sales and net income direction matter.

Nordstrom serves a more affluent customer. Its multichannel and direct sales significantly outperform, showing that technology and inventory integration can improve execution. It is not proof that Penney can instantly import Nordstrom's customer economics. Nordstrom Rack comparable sales declined 0.9%, reminding investors that formats within one company may diverge.

The investable question is how much of this peer gap is fixable within Penney's existing brand/customer franchise. Assortment speed, exclusive merchandise, labor productivity and inventory turns are plausible levers; changing the customer's basic shopping behavior is a more speculative undertaking.

Date-matched peer multiples, sales per square foot and normalized rent/pension-adjusted margin tables are not extracted. No fabricated precise upside benchmark is supplied. The observed sales gap is enough to identify a problem; it is not itself a validated turnaround plan or evidence that peak historical margins will return.
docs.D07_recent_event_timeline.md:
Title: New brands, weak quarterly guidance and a better August
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1166126/000116612610000040/jcpenney10q2nd2010.htm; https://sgbonline.com/jc-penney-posts-2q-profit-but-outlook-disappoints/; https://wwd.com/business-news/retail/penneys-dillards-swing-back-to-black-both-see-sales-declines-3216853/; https://www.cnbc.com/2010/09/02/retailers-post-surprisingly-strong-august-sales.html
Date: 2010-09-10

**March30 — FY2009 annual report.** The filing documents another sales decline, lower reported operating profitability and substantial pension expense. Cash generation improved as capex fell and inventory was reduced. The report establishes both financial runway and the need to separate operating performance from pension accounting.

**May — debt tender.** The Q2 filing describes a debt repurchase/tender that produces US$20 million bond premiums and unamortized-cost expense during the quarter. Repaying debt consumes cash but reduces future financing obligations; the one-time EPS effect is not an ordinary merchandise cost.

**July31 — Q2 closes.** Inventory is US$3.490 billion, approximately 7.1% above the year-earlier balance, while quarterly sales are virtually unchanged. Cash remains US$2.003 billion and long-term debt US$3.099 billion.

**August13 — earnings/outlook.** JCP returns to a modest profit of US$0.06 per share but projects US$0.16–US$0.20 Q3 EPS and US$1.40–US$1.50 full-year EPS, below contemporary analyst expectations. Shares close at US$19.82 according to WWD.

**August — brand rollouts.** Management discusses 77 initial MNG by Mango shops, expanded Liz Claiborne merchandise and planned Call It Spring footwear shops. The programs are intended to strengthen exclusivity and fashion appeal. They also create inventory, execution and brand-coordination obligations.

**September2 — monthly sales.** August comparable sales increase 2.3%, exceeding the 1.6% estimate reported by CNBC. Macy's, Kohl's and Nordstrom still show larger comparable gains. Industry promotions and school-related spending contribute to the improvement.

**September — detailed quarterly filing.** Investors can inspect the full pension, cash, inventory and financing disclosures rather than rely only on the profit headline. First-half operating cash flow is negative US$379 million, emphasizing seasonality and working-capital needs.

The next observable tests are September/holiday sales, merchandise gross margin, inventory clearance and response to new labels. There is no established externally imposed deadline for a management replacement or corporate restructuring. A shareholder may propose changes, but the investment cannot assume the board has agreed. No post-cutoff stakeholder, operating experiment or outcome is included in this timeline.
docs.D08_pershing_square_context.md:
Title: Existing retail exposure and asset-value activism
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1336528/0001172661-10-000510.txt; https://pdfcoffee.com/pershing-square-q2-10-investor-letter-pdf-free.html; https://rationalwalk.com/bill-ackman-to-speak-at-nyc-value-investing-congress/
Date: 2010-08-26

The June30 13F, filed August16, reports US$3.502028 billion public-equity value. It is not firmwide AUM, fund cash or a complete economic portfolio. Several positions use derivatives or involve nonpublic/other capital not fully reflected in this table.

| Aggregated long common holding | Reported value, US$m | Approximate table weight |
|---|---:|---:|
| Target | 1,016.845 | 29.0% |
| Kraft | 942.226 | 26.9% |
| Citigroup | 550.840 | 15.7% |
| Automatic Data Processing | 332.951 | 9.5% |
| General Growth Properties | 317.627 | 9.1% |
| Corrections Corporation | 208.672 | 6.0% |
| Yum | 74.456 | 2.1% |
| Landry's | 38.017 | 1.1% |
| Borders | 14.096 | 0.4% |
| Greenlight Capital Re | 6.298 | 0.2% |

Values sum sole/shared rows once. The sizeable existing Target exposure and smaller Borders holding matter when considering additional department-store/consumer risk. Real-estate experience does not make different retail formats or customers interchangeable.

The August26 investor letter, available as a third-party archival transcription, says Yum was sold as its price approached estimated intrinsic value. It describes Landry's as a catalyst opportunity arising from a going-private offer and the outcome of negotiations. It discusses General Growth and other portfolio situations. These are dated examples of value-oriented sales and engagement, not a newly disclosed JCP thesis.

An August24 Rational Walk report attributes “over US$3 billion” AUM to the Value Investing Congress organizers. This is too imprecise and potentially narrow to reconcile firmwide NAV or investable cash; no exact AUM is asserted in meta. AUM should not be substituted with the conveniently available 13F total.

An activist can recruit expertise, seek board influence and press for accountability, but cannot guarantee that customers accept a new assortment or proposition. Existing ownership of Target demonstrates prior retail analysis, not proof of skill in a different turnaround. No authenticated pre-September24 Ackman JCP statement is available. The pack therefore evaluates public fit and capacity before public disclosure, without importing a future executive recruitment or operating plan.

drivers.driver: Recover an underperforming department-store franchise's sales productivity and profitability using a large existing asset base.
Recruit exceptional retail leadership; actual Ron Johnson recruitment occurred in2011, not as a completed fact at entry.
Change merchandising/customer proposition and board accountability, but execution and customer behavior proved much less predictable than expected.
drivers.quote: too much change too quickly without adequate testing on what the impact would be

drivers.driver: Sought faster CEO succession and chairman change after the turnaround failed; a later crisis response, not an original2010 assumption.
drivers.quote: I think JC Penney is at a very critical stage in its history and its very existence is at risk.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Eight dated documents. Strong pre-entry financial/peer evidence, owned-property count, pension normalization and competing merchandising/structural interpretations. Dates explicitly pre-disclosure not pre-first-buy. Exact original pitch, NAV sizing, rolling price extrema, independent property appraisal, peer valuation and full signed investor-letter postmortem remain gaps. Later CEO, pricing experiment and collapse confined to key.

valuation.eps_path: Stagnant or declining due to structural headwinds
valuation.downside_case: Permanent loss of capital if margin compression continues and market share is permanently ceded to competitors.

drivers.driver: The business is experiencing a structural decline in department store relevance and traffic that has not been reversed [D01].
Operating margins have severely compressed, falling from 9.5% in 2007 to 3.8% in 2009 [D02].
The company faces intense competitive pressure from discount stores, fast-fashion chains, and online retailers [D05].
We have identified no actionable catalyst or turnaround plan that would justify an investment at the current 17.0–18.3x forward P/E multiple [D01, D04].

kill_criteria: management abandons the exclusive brand and shop-in-shop growth strategy
comparable store sales remain negative for two consecutive quarters
operating margins fail to recover toward historical averages
inventory-to-sales ratio continues to trend adversely, indicating sustained markdown risk
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A demonstrated, executable strategy to reverse margin compression and evidence that the decline in store traffic is cyclical rather than secular.
final.memo:
The Company is a large-scale department-store retailer with over 1,100 locations offering a mix of private and national brands [D01]. While the company maintains a significant physical footprint, it currently fails to meet our criteria for a simple, predictable, and free-cash-flow-generative business [D01, D02].

The opportunity as presented is marred by a structural decline in department store relevance that the market has correctly identified [D01]. The company has suffered two consecutive years of declining sales and a significant contraction in operating margins from 9.5% in 2007 to 3.8% in 2009 [D02].

At a forward P/E of 17.0–18.3x based on 2010 guidance, the stock is not priced for the reality of its deteriorating competitive position [D04]. We believe the valuation is expensive given the lack of a clear earnings growth algorithm and the potential for further multiple compression toward 10x [D01, D04].

We pass on this investment because we cannot identify a catalyst for value creation or a concrete plan to reverse the structural headwinds [D01, D05]. Without a defined activist strategy to drive transformation, we cannot advocate for an investment in the current climate [D01, D05].

Risks remain high, primarily centered on the potential for permanent capital loss if market share continues to be ceded to online and off-price competitors [D01, D05]. Our focus remains on higher-quality compounders where the path to long-term value is more clearly defined [D01].

Consequently, we have elected to PASS on this opportunity and will not initiate a position [D01, D05].

valuation.eps_path: Stagnant/Declining due to lack of turnaround catalyst [D01]
valuation.downside_case: Significant permanent loss likely if margins continue to compress toward zero and structural relevance is lost [D01, D05]

drivers.driver: The business faces structural competitive pressure from fast-fashion and discounters, leading to a loss of relevance with moderate-income consumers [D01, D05].
Operating margins have experienced significant compression, falling from 9.5% in 2007 to 3.8% in 2009 [D02].
Returns on beginning invested capital have declined sharply from 15.7% to 7.8% over two years, indicating poor capital allocation or business decay [D02].
The company lacks a defined outside shareholder operating plan or leadership change necessary to reverse the performance trajectory [D01].

kill_criteria: Continued decline in operating margins below 3% for two consecutive quarters.
Comparable store sales growth consistently trailing the industry average by over 200 basis points.
Inventory growth continuing to outpace sales growth, necessitating permanent margin-dilutive markdowns.
Failure to secure a board-level mandate for comprehensive operational and leadership change within 6 months of initiation.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence of a successful, actionable turnaround plan led by a proven retail operator that demonstrably reverses margin compression and regains market share from competitors.
final.memo:
J.C. Penney is a major U.S. department store retailer operating 1,107 locations with a focus on apparel and home merchandise [D01]. Despite its scale and presence, the business currently fails to meet our criteria for a predictable, high-quality, free-cash-flow-generative franchise due to its declining competitive position [D01, D02, D05].

The opportunity for improvement is hampered by the lack of an actionable turnaround plan or a change in leadership [D01]. The market has correctly identified J.C. Penney as a struggling retailer that has failed to keep pace with fast-fashion and discount store competitors [D01, D05].

At a valuation of 17.0–18.3x 2010 guidance, the stock does not trade at a discount that compensates for the significant risk of permanent impairment as margins continue to compress [D04]. With returns on invested capital falling from 15.7% to 7.8% over the last two years, we see no immediate catalyst to justify an investment [D02].

While we have expertise in the retail sector, J.C. Penney represents a high-risk turnaround without a clear path to value creation [D08]. The structural decline in relevance and the inability of management to stem margin pressure from 9.5% down to 3.8% leads us to pass on this opportunity [D02, D05].
